subject: Senior staff heatcheck — priorities, decisions, and asks for QBR prep
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Senior staff heatcheck — priorities, decisions, and asks for QBR prep

Team — sending a compact heatcheck ahead of tomorrow's leadership sync. I focused this on what needs decisioning for the QBR and any cross-org blockers. Short bullets up front, then asks.

Wins
- Hosted API latency rollout (v1.3) is in production: p50 down ~12% on small models; infra reports stable after last week's kernel patch.
- Three mid-market pilots moved to paid in the last two weeks (net +$35k ARR monthly).

Risks / Open Issues
- Dedicated capacity backlog: potential 3-week provisioning delay for new reservations if we can't secure one additional A100 cluster this month. (Impact: sales-forced deals with dedicated requirement).
- Eval regression flagged on code-gen prompts for model-quantized variant; infra/ops mitigation in progress but we should scope rollback windows.

Asks (concrete)
1) Decision: Approve emergency capacity purchase to cover two Dedicated reservations this quarter (cost estimate in attached spreadsheet). Owner: Laura — needed by EOD Wed.
2) Approve including a headcount ask (1 TAM for enterprise onboarding) in the QBR ask slide. Owner: Laura + Karthik — confirmation by Thu COB.
3) Marissa: confirm customer escalations impacted by the code-gen regression are triaged with remediation ETA. Please include affected accounts in reply.

Attached: QBR-Prep-heatcheck.xlsx (costs & capacity runbook), org-priorities-1pager.pdf
Links: draft QBR pulse deck https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRPulseDraft, Jira OPS-1427

Thanks —
David
David Kim
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior staff heatcheck — priorities, decisions, and asks for QBR prep

Thanks David — quick clarifying question on the Dedicated capacity ask. The attached spreadsheet assumes a best-case procurement lead time of 10 business days; if we land at +3 weeks, does the cost delta change materially (licensing / temporary burst capacity)?

Also, on the eval regression: can the applied rollback be scoped to only the quantized variant while keeping v1.3 live? If so, we can avoid wider customer impact.

On customer exposure: happy to jump into any account calls this week if that helps de-risk.

Jonas

Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior staff heatcheck — priorities, decisions, and asks for QBR prep

Agree with the asks. Quick notes / decisions:
- Capacity purchase: approved for the two reservations at the level in the spreadsheet. Finance confirmed we can cover this under the reserved-capex line — move forward. Laura (approved)
- Headcount ask: include 1 TAM in the QBR ask slide; please add a 1-slide justification (KPI impact / ramp plan). Karthik + David, please coordinate and drop the slide in the deck by Thu 9am.

Marissa — please enumerate affected accounts in your reply so I can escalate to Sales leadership if needed. Jonas: work with infra to confirm staging rollback isolation plan for quantized variant; if rollback is isolated we keep v1.3 live.

I'll be at the leadership sync tomorrow and will signal these as approved items; David, present the two asks as bullet requests (capacity + TAM).

Laura
Director, Finance & Ops

Cc: Emma Lawson <emma@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior staff heatcheck — priorities, decisions, and asks for QBR prep

Looping in Emma from Acme — they were impacted by the code-gen regression and asked to join the QBR discussion so we can align on the mitigation timeline and mutual action plan.

Affected accounts (short list):
- Acme Analytics (primary contact: Emma Lawson) — production inference logs show increased token failure rates on quantized variant between 05/02–05/06.
- Medallion Health — CS reported latency spike; root cause appears related to a batching edge-case introduced by the new kernel selection.

Status / next steps:
- Immediate mitigation: roll the quantized inference path to previous model build for impacted customers; infra has a rollback playbook ready (Jira OPS-1427).
- Customer comms: I drafted an account note and will run it by Emma before sending.
- ETA for stabilization: 24–36 hours once rollback starts. I'll update the thread when tickets are closed.

Attachment: ticket-summaries.txt (see Drive link)

Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager

- Karthik + I will drop the 1-slide TAM justification into the deck by Thu 9am (link below).

Updated links: QBR pulse deck (finalize slide in /Section 3/Asks): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRPulseDraft
PO / procurement runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=procurement-runbook

If there are no objections, I'll present the two asks at tomorrow's leadership meeting as approved items and call out the customer impact and rollback plan.

Thumbs up here = go live.

-David
